doc.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Norman Granz's talent for pairing players
summary: Williams recalls a 1973 Yugoslavia episode; Peterson says Granz paired players and set them against each other, as with Roy Eldridge.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: But that’s just one instance. In 1973 now, I’m sitting in a counter in Yugoslavia. I can’t even remember which city it was. Backstage. Because you know they have a place for artists to have a drink and some food backstage. But people from the theater can come back through a door and you can get into the theater through a door. And they were standing there with stacks of LP’s. And I signed each one. And Norman, sitting beside me right here at the bar, and I said, “you know you are very much responsible for this, you know.” Now they didn’t know that I knew that between him, Voice of America and Armed Forces Radio, the stuff like that. Your experiences with him had to be —
He had great insight. Norman had great insight.

Norman Granz had the facility to listen to various players and pair them. And in some cases pit them one against the other. You know he’d, I remember we were listening to one player, I won’t call any names, we were listening to one person play and he’d say, “boy he can play. I’d like to hear him with Little Jazz” you know, Roy Eldridge.

And I’d say, “why?” I say, “why don’t you just do an album with him?” He said, “we’ll do one with him, but you know, I’d like to hear them get together. I’d like to see who’s going to come out — there’s going to be some bloodletting.”
He always saw it that way. And many of the great sessions were produced on that basis.
